subject: Follow-up: Redwood pricing & token economics
messages:
From: Lena Park <lena.park@acme.ai>

Subject: Follow-up: Redwood pricing & token economics

Thanks again for the demo this morning - good overview and the latency numbers looked promising. A quick follow-up from our side with more context so you can help us benchmark pricing and unit economics.

Current state:
- Prod usage today (in our hosted environment): ~25M tokens/month (prompt+completion).
- Traffic profile: ~70% generation (completion heavy), average response length ~350 tokens.
- Growth expectations: target 4x in 6 months (~100M/mo), and 20x in 12 months (~500M/mo) if adoption continues.

Budget and targets:
- Our finance team is modeling a budget range for the next 6-12 months of $5k-$15k/month initially, scaling up as value is proven.
- High-level ask: what unit price /1M tokens should we target to hit our internal target spend? For reference, finance is thinking target effective cost of ~$12-$18 per 1M tokens at scale (post-quantization/optimizations) for inference cost alone.

Request:
1) Can you provide a benchmark comparison $/1M tokens vs OpenAI, Anthropic, and common open-model hosting options (Hugging Face, Replicate, self-host on clouds) for both hosted and dedicated/reserved capacity?
2) What pricing/discounting profile do you have at 100M/mo and 500M/mo?
3) Any detail on how quantization / batch / prefix caching would impact unit economics for our workload?

Happy to share a 2-week sample of logs or a small traffic dump if that helps with a tailored estimate. Looking to schedule a follow-up call next week to review a scoped estimate and a potential trial.

Best,
Lena
Head of Product
Acme AI

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Redwood pricing & token economics

Hi Lena - great to chat yesterday, and thanks for the detailed numbers. Quick recap and an initial benchmarking note (see attached for a pro-forma estimate and a simple token economics worksheet).

Recap:
- Current usage: ~25M/mo, growth to ~100M/mo (6 months) and ~500M/mo (12 months) - got it.
- Budget: $5k-$15k/mo initially; finance target of ~$12-$18 per 1M tokens is helpful context.

Initial benchmarking (very high-level; model/quality variance will change these numbers):
- OpenAI (GPT-4 family): materially higher for large-context, high-quality LLMs - ballpark (for top-tier models) can be multiple hundreds $/1M tokens. GPT-3.5-class models are much cheaper (tens of $/1M).
- Anthropic (Claude family): generally positioned between top OpenAI models and cheaper hosted open-models - order of magnitude higher than open LLM hosting for high-quality models (roughly low hundreds $/1M for Claude-like large models).
- Open-model hosts (Hugging Face managed / Replicate / smaller inference providers): wide range, typically ~$10-$50 per 1M tokens depending on model, quantization, and concurrency. Heavily quantized LLMs on optimized runtimes can push effective inference cost down to single-digit $/1M tokens at very large scale, but quality/latency tradeoffs apply.
- Redwood Hosted (our managed API, using curated open models / verified performance profiles): typically in the $12-$25 per 1M tokens range for workloads like yours (depends on model variant + streaming vs non-streaming).
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity): with committed throughput and optimized quantization we can get closer to ~$6-$12 per 1M tokens at the 100M-500M scale, depending on a few knobs (batching, KV caching hit rate, sequence lengths).

Notes on drivers and what we need:
- Quantization: moving from FP16 to 4-bit/8-bit execution can reduce costs 2-4x depending on kernel support and model.
- Batching & caching: if you have a lot of repeated prefixes / templates we typically see 20-40% effective token savings via prefix caching and smarter batching.
- Model selection: smaller distilled variants may reduce cost significantly while preserving acceptable quality for many use cases.

Attachments: Redwood-pricing-estimate-ACME-20260322.xlsx (simple cost model for 25M / 100M / 500M scenarios) and token-economics-worksheet.csv (template to drop sample traffic).

Proposed next steps:
1) You share a 2-week sample (anonymized) traffic CSV (use the attached worksheet layout) - we can run it against our benchmark harness to give a tailored $/1M estimate.
2) Aditya (cc) will help set up a short perf benchmark for a few model variants (quantized and baseline) and confirm throughput/latency numbers for your response lengths.
3) We prepare a draft commercial for Redwood Hosted vs Redwood Dedicated (including commit tiers at 100M and 500M) and review on a follow-up call next week.

Would Monday or Tuesday next week work for a 30-min review? I can block time; Vanessa, Aditya - can you confirm availability for Wed-Fri if earliest is not possible?

Thanks - talk soon.

- Marissa
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
